searchText: How blocks formatting would be addressed? I have compared blocks between some of the clients and are different (format). May be a get_standard_block API ? (By Previously Defining block standard formatting). Blocks containing different sets of properties is one of the many things that different between clients. There should be a set of things that all clients provide at least though. I understand that. And Thats great. I was just referring to an API that regardless the client return a block into standard formatting (whatever it would be) and may be points out what is the “additional” that each specific client “provides” against it. That is what the linked API wants to do eventually, but it needs someone to actually do the work of figuring out what exactly each client returns and document that. (Question:) Should this be a PR ? , I have done some observations between geth and nethermind, it is really interesting btw. ^ If you want to contribute, I think it would be appreciated. <@543900561460822016> may have ideas on how to express cross-client differences in the spec. As usual: thanks for your feedback Micah. <@834543635587924028> I have a set of tests running against all clients that show their deviations from geth here: https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/ checkout the `rpc-compat` test results! ideally, there should be no difference across clients so if you see them, it would be great to determine which client is "right" and raise the issue with the "wrong" client and potentially issue a spec change Great ! I will take a look on it ! Wonderful. Thanks! This is often non-trivial. 😖 Nothing is trivial. Those are your words. But that’s the original question what is standard or right for block formatting ? Where is defined ? Any EIP ? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis I know but is this not basically geth ? geth afaict adheres to this there have been some small changes in geth along the way, but generally the spec represents what geth has implemented Ok. So what about the rest of the clients ? I think what <@834543635587924028> is getting at is that Getting doesn't return the same thing as Nethermind (for example) and the specs currently are just "what geth does". Will these specs be taken as standard ? So the question is, how do we express the different structures in the spec, so it is clear to users where the differences are? Exactly. That’s the whole idea of standardization. I mean, the goal should be no differences? Sure, but step one is identifying the differences. Step two is deciding which is correct (hard problem). Step 3 is updating clients to match decision from 2 (slow problem). I understand it. But who defined ? We are still on step 0 effectively (we haven't started step 1). And these should be a PR. ! It's been defined by many client devs and EIPs over the last 7 years What has been defined? the API 4 different APIs have been defined.
